findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses a Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree) to count strictly smaller values on both sides of each index. In the first pass (left-to-right), it records smaller_left[i] = query(nums[i] - 1) and adds nums[i] to the tree. In the second pass (right-to-left), it checks query(nums[i] - 1) >= k and smaller_left[i] >= k. The solution runs in O(n log n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.
Querying at nums[i] - 1 counts values strictly smaller than nums[i]. Performing two independent Fenwick passes correctly calculates left-side and right-side smaller element counts for every index.

Each of the n elements requires O(log n) Fenwick query and update operations in both passes, giving O(n log n) total time and O(n) auxiliary space for the tree and smaller_left array. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts nums array and integer k, returning total count of k-big indices.

The approach accurately details order statistic queries, Fenwick tree coordinate mapping (1 to n), dual pass structure, and O(n log n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover direct side scans, merge-sort counting, strict inequality query adjustments, side boundary limits, and monotone arrays.
